description:
Get what the ads cost and what they really brought in over a day range: ad spend, the conversions and the sales value each ad platform claims, the real sales, and the ratios Well computes from them. Use it for ROAS, cost per order, revenue per visit, conversion rate, or spend against sales; use `well_list_daily_metrics` for raw daily rows.

`totals` holds the window. `real_sales` is what the store and the invoices really sold, net of tax, each sale counted once (A paid sales order counts, its unpaid rest is owed.); `paid_orders` counts those sales: each paid store order, and each issued invoice whether or not it is paid. `claimed_conversions` and `claimed_sales_value` are what the platforms claim: never revenue, and they can count one sale twice across platforms. `ratios` are computed, never stored: `blended_roas` = real sales / spend, `claimed_roas` = claimed sales value / spend, `cost_per_paid_order` = spend / paid orders. State a figure as the tool returns it; never recompute or add it.

`visits_by_source` lists each analytics source's visits on its own, never added together, each with `revenue_per_visit` = real sales / that source's visits and `conversion_rate` = paid orders / that source's visits (a fraction, 0.0159 is 1.59 %). Each carries its `definition` (what it counts), or `unknown`. `visits_comparable` is true only when two or more sources state the same definition; otherwise their definitions differ or are unknown, so state each source's visits as its own figure and never add them.

Money is per currency and never converted. A null figure or ratio was not measured: it is never zero. `missing` says why: `no_source_rows` (no connected source reported it), `no_sales_source` (no store or invoicing tool connected), `not_attributable` (orders and visits name no campaign, ad account or channel, so those groups carry spend and claims only), `sales_read_truncated`, `several_currencies` (no ratio across currencies), `source_stale` (a source feeding the figure is not fresh enough, so the ratios built on it are null: never read its figure as complete), `unreadable_sales_rows` (some sales rows have no net amount or no currency, so real sales leave them out), `unreadable_sales_check_failed` (that check could not run, so say real sales may leave some rows out). When `ad_spend` is null and `other_levels_with_spend` names a level, call again with that `level`.

Each connected source in `ad_sources`, `sales_sources` and `visits_sources` gives `synced_at`, `fresh_enough` and `window_rows` (`none` when it wrote nothing for the window, for example a source that stopped syncing): when a source is not fresh enough, say its figures may be old, and offer `well_request_sync` with its id. `window.partial_day` true means the window ends today, so today's figures are still coming in. The latest days may still change even when the window ended: platforms restate recent days, and a platform's day can follow another timezone than the workspace's. `sales_side_unknown` true means the workspace's own company is unknown and real sales may include purchases. `groups_truncated` true means more than 200 groups: narrow the range before you rank them.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

from_date.description: The first day, as YYYY-MM-DD, included.

group_by.description: Split the window: source (each ad account), project (each campaign, ad set or ad of the level), traffic_channel, or day (at most 31 days). The totals only when absent.

level.description: The level the ad figures are read at: campaign (default), ad_set or ad. One level per call.

to_date.description: The last day; the window holds at most 400 days, both ends included, as YYYY-MM-DD, included.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_get_ad_performance

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.
